title: Broken: a cast quietly turns amounts into NULLs
objective_text: Find and fix a silent data cleaning bug: a try_cast that turns formatted amounts into NULL.
scenario: The payments load stopped failing a month ago, after someone changed its cast to try_cast. Since then finance's revenue report has been less than half of what the payment provider says. Nobody has touched the report. Find where the money went and fix the load.
engine_label: DuckDB's PySpark API on this PC (not Apache Spark)
starting_environment: A Delta table bronze.payments (8 payments, amount as text) and the broken job as answer.py.

fault.summary: try_cast reads only plain numbers, so every amount with $ or a thousands separator becomes NULL.
fault.symptom: silver.payments has NULL amounts for payments that had one, and revenue is far too low; the job never fails.
fault.planted: The job casts the raw text with try_cast and cleans nothing first.

required: Every amount that is a number once $, commas and spaces are removed becomes that number, as decimal(12,2).
Blank amounts and values that aren't amounts (N/A, unknown) are NULL, never 0.
Write silver.payments with payment_id and amount, so that running the code again leaves the same table.

expected.description: silver.payments has 8 rows; only p5 (blank) and p6 (N/A) have a NULL amount, and p7 is 2000.00.

verifies: Your fixed job keeps every readable amount and only real unknowns as NULL, on the exercise data and on rows you haven't seen, on this PC.
Running it again leaves the same table.
does_not_verify: It doesn't run on Apache Spark or in a Databricks workspace, so it doesn't show how cast behaves there with ANSI mode on or off.
hints: Run the job and look at which rows have a NULL amount in silver.payments. What do their bronze values have in common?
try_cast can't read '$75.25' or '1,250.50'. Remove $, commas and spaces before casting: regexp_replace(amount, '[$, ]', '').
A blank left after cleaning should be NULL: nullif(..., ''). Keep try_cast for N/A, and don't turn NULLs into 0.
explanation: try_cast hid the failure instead of fixing it: every value with a currency sign or a thousands separator became NULL. Clean the text first by removing $, commas and spaces, turn an empty result into NULL, and only then try_cast to decimal(12,2), so that only values that really aren't amounts stay NULL. Replacing those with 0 would report payments that never happened.
troubleshooting: '$75.25' is still NULL: the cleaning removes commas but not the currency sign.
'$ 10.00' is still NULL: the cleaning keeps the space after the sign.
N/A became 0.00: a missing amount isn't a zero amount; leave it NULL.
reset: Reset rebuilds bronze.payments from setup.sql, removes silver.payments and puts the broken job back.
cleanup: Everything lives in this exercise's folder on this PC; Reset or removing the exercise deletes it. Nothing is created in any workspace.
